_note: This is the config the DEV profile loads — the dry-run harness against `.env`. The file under tests/fixtures/governor/ is frozen golden reference data for the GB-C suite: its numbers were chosen so each fixture sits unambiguously on one side of a threshold, and changing one retroactively invalidates 20 hand-authored verdicts. The two are therefore separate files on purpose. THE DUPLICATION IS REAL AND IS A KNOWN DEBT: every number below except max_expiry_date exists twice, and the resolution is ONE calibrated config that both the suite and the run read, which is a both-humans decision because it changes what the golden fixtures mean. Until then, GB-C-F07 asserts the two files agree on every shared key, so a drift is a test failure rather than a discovery. The SCORED COMPETITION account does NOT read this file — it reads config/thresholds.competition.json, selected by config/profiles.json from the env file the run named.
_max_expiry_rationale: DECIDED 2026-09-02. Scoring reads TOTAL ACCOUNT EQUITY at EOD Thursday 2026-09-03, with that day's option exercises and assignments reflected (EVENT_FACTS.md, Alpaca FAQ, [primary] verified). A short premium position still open after the bound is scored at its MARK — unrealised and moving — rather than at the premium collected. Positions that resolve on or before 2026-09-03 convert premium into scored equity instead of leaving mark-to-market residue in the number the judges read. The governor rejects any proposal with a leg expiring after this date (x_max_expiry), and the data layer's fetch window is clamped to it so a late contract never enters the pipeline. This is a SCORED-RUN BOUND, not a trading judgement.

max_loss_cap._note: Per structure, in dollars, for the whole order (multiplier and qty applied). covered_call is null: a covered call's downside is the share position it is written against, bounded by the coverage check (GB_INTERFACES.md 2e), not by a standalone max-loss figure.

_x_total_open_risk_note: PROPOSED, added 2026-09-02 with the check itself. The portfolio-level cap on the sum of the governor's own computed max loss across every ledger position bearing risk, plus the proposal's. Per-structure caps bound one trade; four trades each inside their own cap can still put the account at risk. Inherited verbatim from the suite's reference config, like every other number here, and held identical to it by GB-C-F07. A number is dollars; the percentage-of-equity form this check also accepts is what the scored account uses.

liquidity_window._status: PROPOSED — not calibrated. Read by the HARNESS's proposal helper, not by the governor: it narrows which contracts a proposal may be built from, and narrowing the candidate set is a strategist's job, not a risk gate's. Held identical to the competition profile's window on purpose, so a dev rehearsal exercises the same code path with the same numbers as the scored run. `null` or absent would mean no window, which the harness states rather than passing silently.
